project_summary.intent: Close the FR-022 gap left by the network-monitoring rollout. The alert engine can already observe WAN, DNS, latency, loss, and public-IP state via FR-016/018/021/026 but never produces a notification for any of them. Add network rule types, a sustained-duration parameter (which also closes BG-037 host-rule flapping), and the settings UI to manage them — reusing the existing Telegram/email channels.
project_summary.north_star_kpi: Percentage of operator-perceptible network incidents (WAN outage, sustained loss >5% for >=120s, sustained latency above target threshold, DNS-resolver failure, public-IP change) that produce exactly one Telegram alert within 1 minute of the incident start — target >=95% on the home lab, measured against ultron-ap.service journal correlated with FR-018/FR-021/FR-026 events.
project_summary.jtbd: When my home internet is actually broken — not flapping, not silent — tell me on Telegram once, with enough context that I know whether to drive home and reboot the router.
project_summary.guardrail_metric: Existing host alert rules (CPU/RAM/Disk/Temp, Docker, Systemd) MUST continue to fire on the same conditions and with the same latency they have today; sustained_duration defaults to 0 for migrated rows so legacy behavior is byte-identical until an operator opts in.
project_summary.scope_anchor: FR-022 acceptance criteria from features/network-monitoring/spec/01_REQUIREMENTS.json, plus BG-037 (flapping) and BG-039 (FR-022 split) in spec/BUGS.json.

user_personas.goal: Be paged on Telegram (and optionally email) within one minute of a real network incident at home, with enough context to act, without being woken up by single-tick blips.
user_personas.pain_point: Ultron-AP already collects WAN/DNS/latency/public-IP telemetry but the alert engine ignores those metrics, so the operator either misses incidents entirely or relies on Telegram traffic from rule_id=11 that flaps every 15–20 minutes (BG-037).

functional_requirements.title: Sustained-latency network alert rule type
functional_requirements.description: Extend the alert engine to evaluate latency rules of the shape `metric=latency`, `target=<host>`, `operator`, `threshold` (milliseconds), `sustained_duration` (seconds). The engine reads RTT samples from the FR-016 gateway probe / FR-018 WAN probe ring buffer and fires exactly one alert when every sample within the trailing `sustained_duration` window satisfies the operator/threshold, respecting the existing per-rule cooldown.
acceptance_criteria: Engine recognises metric=latency in AlertConfig and accepts target in {gateway, 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1} (FR-016 configured target list) — unknown targets are rejected at rule create time with HTTP 400

Given threshold=100, operator='>', sustained_duration=120: when every RTT sample for >=120s is >100ms, exactly one alert is created on the transition and no further alert is created for the next 15 minutes (existing cooldown)
Given any sample within the 120s window is <=100ms: no alert is created — the sustained window resets on the offending sample
Failure path — sample stream gap >2 ticks (ultron-ap restarted, monitor stalled): the sustained window resets and does not produce a stale alert against pre-restart samples

functional_requirements.title: Sustained packet-loss network alert rule type
functional_requirements.description: Same shape as FR-071 with metric=loss, threshold in percentage (0–100). Reads loss percentage from the same FR-016 probe samples.
acceptance_criteria: Engine recognises metric=loss with operator/threshold/target and uses the same sustained-window evaluator as FR-071

Given threshold=5, operator='>', sustained_duration=60, target=gateway: when loss%>5 for every sample in the trailing 60s, exactly one alert is created; alert body includes target, current loss% and configured threshold
Given alternating samples around the threshold: no alert is created (the window only fires when the entire window is in breach)
Cooldown — same 15-minute default as host rules; per-rule override honoured

functional_requirements.title: DNS-resolver failure-rate alert rule type
functional_requirements.description: metric=dns_failure_rate, threshold in percentage. Reads failure rate from the FR-016 DNS probe over the trailing `sustained_duration` window. One rule covers all configured resolvers — the alert body names the resolver with the worst rate.
acceptance_criteria: Engine recognises metric=dns_failure_rate with no target (the rule observes all configured resolvers as one population)

Given threshold=20, operator='>', sustained_duration=120: when the configured resolvers' aggregate failure rate is >20% for every sampled tick in the trailing 120s, exactly one alert fires; the body names the resolver(s) that contributed
Given <2 DNS samples observed in the window (resolver list empty / probe disabled): the rule is skipped and no alert is created — observability log line records the skip with reason
Cooldown — existing 15-minute default applies

functional_requirements.title: WAN outage transition alerts (critical fire + info resolve)
functional_requirements.description: Transition-based, NOT sustained: when the FR-018 outage_start event fires, emit a critical alert immediately; when outage_end fires, emit an info resolve alert. The engine treats this rule like the existing Docker/Systemd transition rules — no threshold, no sustained-duration field, just an enabled flag.
acceptance_criteria: Rule type metric=wan_outage has no threshold or operator — only enabled + severity_override(default=critical) + cooldown
Given FR-018 emits outage_start (>=N consecutive failed gateway+resolver probes): a critical alert is fired in the next engine tick with WAN-down body (interfaces, last successful probe timestamp)

Given FR-018 emits outage_end while a previous outage_start is still within the cooldown window: an info resolve alert is fired immediately (existing FR-018 resolve path), the fire counter is reset, and the next outage_start (if any) is not suppressed by the prior cooldown
Given the rule is disabled: neither fire nor resolve is dispatched even when outage events are observed
Persistence — outage_start fires are recorded in alerts table with type=wan_outage; resolve alerts are notification-only (no DB row, matches existing FR-018 resolve semantics)

functional_requirements.title: Public-IP change alert
functional_requirements.description: Transition-based: when FR-026 detects a public IP change, fire one info alert containing the old IP and new IP. Suppress on the first observation after ultron-ap startup (so a fresh DB does not page on every boot).
acceptance_criteria: Rule type metric=public_ip_change has no threshold/operator; severity is fixed at info; cooldown is configurable (default 60 min to suppress carrier IP rotations)
Given FR-026 emits public_ip_changed{old=A, new=B} with A!=B and A is non-empty: one info alert is fired with body containing old=A new=B and the change timestamp
Given ultron-ap starts and FR-026 emits its first observation (old='' new=B): no alert is fired (the engine treats empty old IP as 'no prior observation')
Given the rule is disabled: no alert is fired even when changes are observed

functional_requirements.title: Sustained-duration parameter on all alert rules
functional_requirements.description: Add a `sustained_duration` field (integer seconds, >=0, default 0) to AlertConfig. The field applies to threshold-style rules (FR-004 host rules and FR-071/FR-072/FR-073 network rules). When sustained_duration=0 the engine fires on first breach (legacy behavior — backward compatible). When >0 the engine fires only after every sample in the trailing window is in breach. This single field closes BG-037 (rule_id=11 flapping) for host rules as well.
acceptance_criteria: Host CPU rule with sustained_duration=0 retains identical fire behavior to today (single-tick breach fires immediately) — verified via TC comparing fire count before/after migration on a recorded sample stream
Host CPU rule with sustained_duration=180 only fires after CPU is above threshold continuously for 180s; intermittent breaches reset the window
BG-037 closure — rule_id=11 (the flapping rule) with sustained_duration=300 fires at most once per cooldown window in a recorded 60-minute alternating-breach trace
Failure path — sample gap >2 engine ticks resets the sustained window without firing (covers process restart, monitor stall, time-skew)

functional_requirements.title: Settings alert-rule form supports network metric types
functional_requirements.description: Extend the existing /settings → Alert rules form (FR-058 widgets — segmented severity, chip-preset cooldown, stepper) so the operator can create any rule type defined by FR-071..FR-075 from the same form, without a separate /network sub-page. The metric <select> gains entries for latency / loss / dns_failure_rate / wan_outage / public_ip_change. A target picker becomes visible only when metric ∈ {latency, loss}, populated from the FR-016 configured target list. A sustained-duration stepper becomes visible only when metric is threshold-style (host + latency/loss/dns_failure_rate).
acceptance_criteria: Metric <select> renders exactly these options in this order: cpu, ram, disk, temp, latency, loss, dns_failure_rate, wan_outage, public_ip_change

Selecting metric=latency or loss reveals a target <select> populated from the FR-016 configured target list (server-rendered via template helper, not client-side fetch) — the target field is name='target' and is required for these metrics

Selecting metric ∈ {wan_outage, public_ip_change} hides target, threshold, operator, and sustained-duration fields — only severity (locked to critical for wan_outage, info for public_ip_change) and cooldown remain visible

Sustained-duration stepper is visible for cpu/ram/disk/temp/latency/loss/dns_failure_rate; data-min=0 data-max=3600; default 0; uses the FR-057 stepper widget so chip-preset / arrow-key affordances are preserved
Form submit posts to existing /api/alerts/rules; server returns the same rules-table partial used today for the host rules form, with the new row included

functional_requirements.title: AlertConfig schema extension and forward-only migration
functional_requirements.description: Extend the alert_configs SQLite table with new nullable columns: target TEXT, sustained_duration INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Provide a forward-only migration that adds the columns and backfills sustained_duration=0 / target=NULL for existing rows. metric is widened in code (not in schema) to accept the new string values. No destructive changes.
acceptance_criteria: After migration runs against a v1 DB: ALL existing alert_configs rows have sustained_duration=0 and target=NULL; row count unchanged; existing rules still load and evaluate identically
Migration is idempotent — running it twice produces the same schema and the same row contents; the second run logs 'schema already at target version' and exits 0

Rollback safety — a downgraded ultron-ap binary that does not know about target/sustained_duration still reads rows successfully (extra columns are ignored at the database/sql layer) — verified via test that loads rows with the old AlertConfig struct
Failure path — migration fails to apply (disk full, schema lock): ultron-ap refuses to start with a clear error and the engine does not enter a partially-migrated state

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Network rule evaluation must add <=50ms per engine tick at the steady-state rule count (currently 11 host rules + up to 10 network rules in the home-lab profile). Measured as p95 of evaluate() wall-time across 60 ticks under load.
acceptance_criteria: p95 evaluate() wall-time with 10 network rules + 11 host rules is <=50ms on Raspberry Pi 4B (ARM Cortex-A72) — measured by an unit benchmark in internal/alerts that replays a recorded sample stream
Memory overhead of sustained-window ring buffers is <=1MB total for 21 rules at 5s tick × 3600s max sustained_duration

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Sustained-window state is process-local and intentionally NOT persisted — on ultron-ap restart, all sustained windows reset to empty. This is correct behavior (the engine cannot vouch for samples it did not observe) and must be tested explicitly so a future change does not silently introduce false-positive fires from stale buffers.
acceptance_criteria: On engine.Start() the firingFirst/sustained-window maps are empty regardless of prior state
A rule with sustained_duration=300 does not fire within the first 300s post-restart even if the metric is in continuous breach during that window — observability log line records the warmup state

non_functional_requirements.requirement: POST /api/alerts/rules validates target strings against the FR-016 configured target list at rule-create time, rejecting unknown values with HTTP 400. The endpoint must NOT execute or echo unsanitised user input (no shell-out to ping for validation, no template rendering of the raw target without HTML escaping).
acceptance_criteria: POST with metric=latency and target='8.8.8.8; rm -rf /' returns 400 'invalid target' — verified by test
POST with metric=latency and target=$(any value NOT in the FR-016 configured list) returns 400 — the validator is whitelist-only, never blacklist
Rendered alert body containing an attacker-controlled target survives Telegram MarkdownV2 escape (reuses BG-036 escape helper)

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Every network-rule evaluation emits the same 9-field structured log line shape used by FR-004 host rules (NFR-007), so journalctl filters that exist today keep working for the new rule types.
acceptance_criteria: A network rule evaluation produces a single-line log: ts=<rfc3339> rule_id=<n> metric=<m> target=<t|-> value=<v> threshold=<th> sustained=<s> in_window=<bool> fired=<bool>
Resolve events (wan_outage_end) produce a matching ts=<rfc3339> rule_id=<n> metric=wan_outage event=resolve duration=<s> line

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Existing host alert rule behavior is preserved byte-for-byte for rows migrated with sustained_duration=0 — no regression in fire timing, alert body, persistence, or notification dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A replay test loads a known CPU sample stream and asserts the engine produces the identical alert rows pre- and post-migration when sustained_duration=0
A goldenfile test of the rendered Telegram body for a host CPU alert is unchanged after the schema migration

acceptance_criteria.given: a v1 DB with 11 existing host rules
acceptance_criteria.when: the new binary starts and runs the migration
acceptance_criteria.then: all 11 rows are present, each with sustained_duration=0 and target=NULL, and a second start logs 'schema already at target version'

acceptance_criteria.given: the post-migration DB is opened by an older ultron-ap binary that lacks target/sustained_duration in AlertConfig
acceptance_criteria.then: loading succeeds — the extra columns are ignored — and the older engine evaluates the rules with legacy semantics

no_go_zone: No new notification channels — Telegram (FR-005) and email (FR-006) remain the only dispatch channels. No webhooks, no SMS, no push, no Discord, no Slack. Adding a channel is a separate FR.
No multi-target rules — one target per latency/loss rule. The operator who needs both gateway and 8.8.8.8 creates two rules. A future FR may introduce target-groups but it is not in this delivery.
No speedtest-driven alerts — speedtest cadence and bandwidth-degradation rules are explicitly excluded. They depend on a separate probe that is not in scope.
No auto-suggested or template rules — the form is manual entry only. No 'recommended threshold' nudges, no rule presets, no 'one-click healthy-home setup'.
No /network sub-page for alert rule management — the existing /settings → Alert rules form is the only surface. The /network page may LINK to /settings but does not duplicate the form.
No re-architecture of the existing FR-004 host alert path — host CPU/RAM/Disk/Temp evaluation code is reused as-is; sustained_duration is layered on top, not refactored under it.
No per-target threshold ladders — a single rule has one threshold. Hysteresis is expressed via sustained_duration, not via separate fire/resolve thresholds.
No persistence of sustained-window state across restarts — windows reset on engine startup. This is correct behavior, not a TODO.
constraints: Single-binary Go server — no new runtime dependencies (no Python/Node, no separate worker, no Redis).
linux/arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4B) is the canonical deploy target; performance budgets in NFR-033 apply to that hardware.
Forward-only SQLite migrations — no destructive ALTERs, no DROP COLUMN, no row rewrites of existing rules.
Reuses existing /api/alerts/rules POST endpoint and existing rules-table partial — no new HTML endpoints.
Reuses FR-058 settings widgets (segmented, chip-preset, stepper) and the BG-038 always-loaded widget JS — no new widget scripts.
technology_preferences: Sustained-window evaluator implemented in internal/alerts as a per-rule ring buffer keyed by rule_id, sharing the pattern already used by internal/insights/lang sustainedSpec — copy the pattern, do not import the package (alerts engine must not depend on insights).

Target list source: read once from the FR-016 configuration at template-render time; do not fetch via SSE or htmx. A reload is acceptable when targets change because target changes are rare and operator-initiated.
Migration framework: continue using the existing in-tree migration runner (no goose/golang-migrate). Migrations live alongside the existing ones in internal/database.
original_brief:
## Feature
Network-class alert rules in the existing alert engine — landing the FR-022
gap left by network-monitoring (engine + UI + sustained-duration hysteresis).

## Problem / Why
FR-022 already specifies sustained latency, sustained loss, WAN outage,
DNS-resolver failure rate, and public-IP-change alerts routed through the
existing Telegram/email channels. The implementation never landed:
- `isValidMetric` in [handlers_settings.go:82](internal/server/handlers_settings.go#L82-L88) only accepts `cpu/ram/disk/temp`.
- [alerts/engine.go](internal/alerts/engine.go) has zero references to latency / loss / DNS / WAN / public_ip.
- Alert-rule form in [settings.html](web/templates/settings.html) only offers the four host metrics.
- BG-037 (rule_id=11 flapping every 15–20 min) is the user-visible symptom of the missing sustained-duration parameter — same root cause, fixed here.

This is the last unresolved gap from the network-monitoring rollout, and the
only thing keeping a network operator from getting paged on a real WAN
incident from Ultron-AP itself.

## Target Users
Raspberry Pi Operator — same persona as FR-022. Wants WAN/DNS/latency
incidents to page Telegram/email like CPU/RAM/temp already do, without
flapping.

## New Behavior
The system must:
- Evaluate `latency_<target>` rules: fire when RTT to a configured target
  exceeds `threshold` for >= `sustained_duration` seconds (default 300s),
  respect the existing 15-minute cooldown.
- Evaluate `loss_<target>` rules: same shape, on packet-loss percentage.
- Evaluate `dns_failure_rate` rules: fire when resolver failure-rate
  exceeds threshold for sustained-duration.
- Fire a `critical` alert on FR-018 WAN `outage_start`; fire an `info`
  resolve when WAN comes back.
- Fire an `info` alert on FR-026 public-IP change carrying old + new IP.
- Accept `sustained_duration` (seconds, integer >= 0) on every alert rule
  via a stepper widget in the settings form. Existing host rules treat
  the field as optional — `0` means "fire on first breach", preserving
  current behavior. This single field also closes BG-037 for host rules.
- Extend the metric `<select>` in the alert-rule form with the new
  network metric types; show a target picker when a target-scoped metric
  is selected.
- Persist the new fields via the existing `/api/alerts/rules` endpoint
  (extend `database.AlertConfig`, add a migration that defaults
  `sustained_duration=0` for existing rows).
- Render the new rules in the existing alerts panel with the same
  severity colour tokens, with no new dispatch channel.

## Success Criteria
- Given a latency rule with `target=8.8.8.8`, `threshold=100ms`,
  `sustained_duration=120s`, when RTT exceeds 100ms continuously for
  >= 120s, then a single alert is created (no flapping at 15–20 min
  cadence — closes BG-037).
- Given an existing CPU rule with `sustained_duration=0`, when CPU
  crosses threshold for one tick, then it fires immediately — backward
  compatibility preserved.
- Given the WAN goes down, when `outage_start` fires, then a `critical`
  alert is emitted within one tick; when it recovers, an `info` resolve
  is emitted.
- Given the public IP changes, when FR-026 detects it, then an `info`
  alert is emitted with both old and new IPs in the body.
- The settings alert-rule form lets the operator create any of the new
  rule types end-to-end and persists them in `alert_configs`.

## Out of Scope
- New notification channels — keep Telegram/email only.
- Multi-target rules (one target per rule).
- Speedtest-driven alerts (separate FR).
- Auto-suggested rule presets / templates.
- Migrating BG-037 host-rule into a per-rule `for_duration` framework
  distinct from `sustained_duration` — they collapse into the same field.
